author: HAI
releaseNotes:
HAI Engine (Preview) 0.5.122: a rule engine for Hubitat, an alternative to Rule Machine, with a rule editor in your browser.

What's new in 0.5.122 (since 0.5.116):

* Away from home: the rule editor and the Migration page now work through Hubitat Remote Access or a VPN. HAI's links follow the address you opened the page with.
* Breaking change for apps that call HAI through the haiRuleApi library: requests are now signed with HAI's API token. Update hai_rule_api.groovy under Libraries code to the new version (printed in docs/developer/api.md), and give the app the API token shown under Rule end points on the HAI Engine page. Until then, HAI ignores its requests and writes a warning to Logs. HAI made a new token when it updated, so an old one no longer works.
* Security: Migration no longer hands out the editor key. The rule end points and the MCP endpoint refuse requests through Hubitat's cloud unless "Allow through Hubitat's cloud" is on (off by default). End points that change something act only on POST; plain GET links work only with "Allow GET links (Rule Machine-style)" on (off by default). A rule's web request cannot reach the hub itself. Rule-to-rule events are signed.
* A caller using Hubitat's cloud address should send Content-Type: application/json, even with an empty body.
* New steps, Reboot the hub and Shut down the hub, under Risky: the whole hub. The editor asks before a rule with one is activated or run, and they work only while "Allow rules to reboot or shut down the hub" is on in HAI Engine. A Rule Machine rule that does this is listed under Risky rules that require your permission on the Migration page, and is copied only with your go-ahead.
* Run rule now works on a stopped rule.
* Reliability: repeated device reports are no longer missed; HAI re-arms itself after an update without you pressing Done; no stray timer jobs are left behind; and HAI puts less load on the hub.
* HAI Engine page: a section you open stays open when you change a toggle inside it, and the end point help is clearer.

This is a preview for invited testers. Expect rough edges, and keep your Rule Machine rules until you trust the HAI copies.

An install or update takes 10 to 15 minutes while the hub compiles the apps. Leave the page open until it finishes; your rules keep running.

* Rule editor: open it from the HAI Engine page. Build rules from triggers, conditions and actions in everyday words, check them, put them on the hub stopped, and start them when ready. Start from a pattern, or open the Showcase rule to see much of what HAI can do.
* AI Rule Assistant (optional): describe a rule in plain words and it drafts one for you to review. It needs your own Claude API key and a spending limit, under AI token and cost management. Everything else works without it.
* Each rule runs as its own small app on the hub, with its run history.
* Backups: a backup of your rules every night, and Back up now at any time. Restore one rule or all.
* HAI Migration (installed, off until you turn it on in HAI Engine): copies Rule Machine rules into HAI one at a time. One page: Assess sorts your rules into can clone, can't clone and empty; Clone makes paused copies; Cut over pauses the Rule Machine rule and starts its copy; Rollback reverses it. Needs Automation Map 2.4.48 or later, with a scan done.
* Off until you switch them on: the MCP endpoint for AI assistants, and the web address for dashboards and shortcuts.

After installing: Apps, Add user app, HAI Engine (Preview). Open the rule editor from its page, check Approved devices, and press Done.

Report a problem or give feedback: More, Report a problem or give feedback in the editor, or the Issues tab of the HAI-Engine repository on GitHub. Report security problems privately, as SECURITY.md explains.
